Working in Sandwich

Working on Sandwich homes.

Sandwich is the oldest town on Cape Cod, and it shows in the houses. Along Route 6A and around the village you'll find antique capes and colonials with original trim profiles worth keeping. In Forestdale and South Sandwich, most homes are newer capes, colonials and ranches where the work is usually decks, siding sections, windows and doors.

Houses near Town Neck, Scorton and the bay side take salt wind off Cape Cod Bay. That's where we see fascia, corner boards and window trim fail first, often with soft sheathing behind them that only shows up once the old board comes off.

Because we're based in town, Sandwich is where small jobs make the most sense for us too: one rotted sill, a door that won't close, a few courses of cedar shingle.

What we check first on Sandwich homes

  • Original trim on older village homes: repair and match before replacing
  • Bay-facing walls: fascia, corner boards and window heads
  • Deck ledgers and stairs on homes built in the 1980s and 90s
  • Doors and windows that drag or leak after years of seasonal movement

Old King's Highway historic district

Much of Sandwich north of Route 6 sits in the Old King's Highway Regional Historic District, where exterior changes visible from a public way generally need approval from the town's historic committee before work starts. We'll flag it at the estimate and plan materials and timing around it.

FAQ

Sandwich questions, answered.

Where is Castro Finish Carpentry located?

Our shop is in Sandwich, MA. We serve all of Sandwich, including the village, East Sandwich, Forestdale and South Sandwich, and the rest of Cape Cod.

Do you take small repair jobs in Sandwich?

Yes. A rotted sill, a sticking door or a few courses of shingle are all worth a call. Being local makes small jobs practical.

Do you work on antique homes in Sandwich Village?

Yes. On older homes we repair and match original trim where it's sound, and replace only what has failed.

Does my project need historic district approval?

If the home is in the Old King's Highway district and the change is visible from a public way, it usually does. We'll tell you at the estimate and plan around the review.
